newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia sets new Bumiputera stock listing rules.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sets new Bumiputera stock listing rules.

text.p: Malaysia's Securities Commission (SC) said on Tuesday it will allow flexibilities in its listing requirements in order to encourage more Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) controlled companies to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
In a statement, the market watchdog said it would allow for listing applications based on proforma accounts for Bumiputera-controlled companies that are grouped together.
In such a grouping, at least one company within the group must fulfill all the applicable listing requirements.

However, if no one company qualified, listing based on the strength of the group's proforma accounts might be considered, provided all companies within the group fulfilled three criteria for at least five years for the main board and at least three years for the Second Board, the SC said.

The criteria are that all the companies be involved in the same business activities; that they have common directors and, that all of them have common shareholders with controlling shareholding on a collective basis.

The company used as a listing vehicle must, upon listing, have more than 50 percent of its equity owned by Bumiputera shareholders and be maintained as a Bumiputera-controlled company, the statement added.
A Bumiputera-controlled company is defined as a company in which more than 50 percent of its equity is owned by Bumiputera shareholders/institutions.

"Between January and July this year, 13 of the 48 companies approved for listing were Bumiputera-controlled companies. In 1995, 16 of the 62 companies approved for listing by the SC were Bumiputera controlled," SC chairman Munir Majid said in the statement.
